LAND ACKNOWLEDGEMENT: We acknowledge that the land on which we are gathered is the
traditional, ancestral, and unceded territory of the Gabrielino/Tongva peoples. We seek to
prioritize respect for the historic culture and contemporary presence of the native peoples
throughout California, especially in the greater Los Angeles/Alhambra area. We come with
respect and gratitude for the Gabrielino/Tongva people who still consider themselves the
caretakers of this land. It is through their examples that we are reminded of our greater

2.  ADOPTION OF THE BICYCLE AND PEDESTRIAN IMPROVEMENT PLAN;
  AUTHORIZATION TO REALLOCATE MEASURE R FUNDS FOR THE
  IMPLEMENTATION OF BICYCLE AND PEDESTRIAN PLAN PROJECTS;
  AUTHORIZATION OF A CONTRACT AMENDMENT WITH ALTA PLANNING FOR
  GRANT SUPPORT SERVICES FOR THE BALANCE OF PLAN IMPROVEMENTS; AND
  ACCEPTANCE OF ENVIRONMENTAL EXEMPTION DETERMINATION – F2M22-33,
  C2M22-39, M2M24-8

  Over the 2023 year, the City of Alhambra, via Alta Planning + Design (Consultant), has
  been working towards the development of a Bicycle and Pedestrian Improvement Plan.
  This Plan is a directive under the City’s Strategic Plan under the goals of Enhancing Public
  Safety, Improving Infrastructure and Mobility, and Promoting Sustainability. Alhambra’s
  Bicycle and Pedestrian Improvement Plan provides opportunity to establish a vision for
  Alhambra’s biking and pedestrian infrastructure. While various components are
  conceptual and subject to additional study and engineering, the Plan provides opportunity
  to establish purpose and need for important transportation mobility changes. Further, the
  Plan strengthens regional collaboration and improves the City’s competitiveness for grant
  funding to enable the City’s proposed projects. To help initiate the Plan’s implementation,
  the Council Subcommittee discussed the possible use of Alhambra’s Measure R Funds,
  which currently are apportioned to various traffic and congestion relief projects throughout
  the City. At the Council’s direction and with Metro’s approval, the funds under this project
  in the amount of $14.4 million could be reallocated to the City’s bicycle and pedestrian
  improvement projects, pending the Council’s approval of the Bicycle and Pedestrian
  Improvement Plan. In addition, the City’s bicycle and pedestrian improvement projects
  can be financed via specified grant sources, particularly those under Caltrans and federal
  resources. Staff is also interested in securing the grant support services of Alta Planning
  + Design to enable immediate consideration of certain grant applications. Grant support
  services, however, are not currently in Alta’s scope of work with the City; therefore, staff
  is recommending an amendment to the agreement between Alta Planning + Design and
  the City to help initiate the development of the City’s grant applications. Finally, staff and
  the Consultant have reviewed the Bicycle and Pedestrian Improvement Plan and
  determined that the improvements contemplated therein are bicycle facilities and
  pedestrian safety improvements that qualify for a Statutory Exemption under California
  Public Resource Code Section 21080.25.

  The Bicycle and Pedestrian Improvement Plan is available for public review via the City’s
  website at https://www.cityofalhambra.org/228/Notices-Documents.

3.  AUTHORIZE RFP: ECONOMIC AND MARKET ANALYSIS CONSULTING SERVICES
  – F2M24-20, RFP2M24-1

  Action Plan. The Plan will create a comprehensive and integrated approach to economic

   development that strengthens the City’s economic base. The vision will focus on the
  community’s present and future economic values over the next four years. Meanwhile,
  the goals will be a more tangible reflection of the vision and provide specific framework to
  implement economic development policies and programs.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council authorized staff to circulate a Request for Proposals

4.  AWARD CONTRACT: PURCHASE OF TWO POLICE PATROL VEHICLES – F2M24-
  6A, C2M24-1, M2M24-2

  In two separate incidents, two police patrol cars were involved in collisions. The repairs of
  both damaged vehicles were beyond the value of the patrol cars. As a result, the Police
  Department is now operating with two fewer vehicles. Staff is seeking to purchase two
  police patrol vehicles to replace the totaled vehicles through a cooperative purchase
  agreement. Cooperative purchase is allowable per Alhambra Municipal Code
  3.36.080(B)(3). On September 15, 2021, Sourcewell opened four bids for procuring
  vehicles, cars, vans, SUVs, and light trucks with related equipment, accessories, and
  services. Sourcewell awarded contract 091521-NAF to National Auto Fleet Group on
  November 4, 2021 - a contract that does not expire until November 8, 2025. Per the
  Sourcewell bid specifications, there is the option of purchasing police vehicles. Staff is
  recommending purchasing two police vehicles utilizing this option.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council awarded a contract, subject to final language approval
  by the City Manager and City Attorney, to National Auto Fleet Group for the purchase of
  two police patrol vehicles in the amount of $100,764.34; directed the Finance Director to
  allocate the insurance payment for the totaled police patrol vehicles in the amount of
  $98,444.00 to account number 507.70.2010.90803; and, directed staff to undertake the
  steps necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M24-2)

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER

   The 2023 Alley Rehabilitation Project (Area A / Phase I) consists of nine alley segments
  located within the City of Alhambra’s boundaries. The alley segments selected to be
  reconstructed are categorized as failed condition in the current Pavement Management
  System Report. The project is located between Ethel Avenue on the West, Valley
  Boulevard on the South, Marengo Avenue on the East, and Front Street on the North.
  City Council authorized the circulation of a Notice Inviting Bids for this project on October
  23, 2023. On November 30, 2023, the City Clerk received six bids that ranged from
  $1,043,640.00 to $1,579,270.00, not including the alternate bid alley segments. Staff
  reviewed the bids and found the bid received from Kalban, Inc. in the amount of
  $1,043,640.00 is the lowest responsible bid. Kalban, Inc. has the necessary licenses to
  complete the work and has conducted similar projects for the City of Alhambra.

  Public Comment:  Joyce Amaro, 1808 S. Sixth St., spoke in support of the item and
  discussed permeable pavement as a possible option for the project.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council awarded a contract, subject to final language approval
  by the City Manager and City Attorney, to Kalban, Inc. in the amount of $1,043,640.00 for
  the 2023 Alley Rehabilitation Project (Area A / Phase I); and, directed staff to undertake
  the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M24-3)

8.  AWARD CONTRACT: PROFESIONAL CONSULTANT SERVICES FOR THE
  DEVELOPMENT OF THE STORY PARK IMPROVEMENT PROJECT – F2M22-37,
  RFP2M22-8, C2M24-4, M2M24-6

  On March 28, 2022, the City Council authorized the circulation of a Request for Proposals
  (RFP) for the Story Park Improvement Project. The Project seeks to convert the vacant
  pool space adjacent to the Joslyn Center into green space and replace the existing
  playground at Story Park with an all-inclusive playground. On September 18, 2023, the
  RFP for the project was posted and circulated. A total of three proposals were received
  from qualified consulting firms. On December 13, 2023, an evaluation panel consisting of
  City staff interviewed and rated the firms to determine how each met the essential
  requirements outlined in the RFP, including compliance with RFP requirements, Project
  understanding and approach, experience, level of effort, schedule, and cost-effectiveness.
  After careful consideration, the evaluation panel determined that KFA Land Images
  Landscape Services best meets the City’s criteria and overall needs.

  Discussion:  Councilmember MALONEY asked if the all-inclusive playground at
  Story Park would be in addition to an all-inclusive playground at Burke Heritage Park,
  noting that an all-inclusive playground at Burke Heritage Park had been previously
  discussed at the Parks & Recreation Commission. Responding, Director of Parks and
  Recreation MACIAS clarified that playgrounds were planned for both locations.

  Action Taken:  City Council awarded a contract, subject to final language approval
  by the City Manager and City Attorney, by and between the City of Alhambra and KFA
  Land Images Landscape Services for professional consultant services for the
  Development of the Story Park Improvement Project in the amount of $236,193.00; and,
  directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M24-6)

  PARKING ON CITY PROPERTY NEAR GARFIELD ELEMENTARY SCHOOL TO THE
  ALHAMBRA UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT – F66-137, C67-32, C2M24-5, M2M24-7

  The Alhambra Unified School District has utilized a portion of City owned land located
  adjacent to the Garfield Elementary School for parking since 1967. Recently, Denise
  Jaramillo, the Superintendent of the Alhambra Unified School District, requested the lease
  be renewed. There is no cost to the City for the Alhambra Unified School District’s
  continued use of the land, as such it is recommended that the lease be continued at no
  fee.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council authorized the City Manager to execute a renewal of a

10.  NOTICE INVITING BIDS: ENVIRONMENTAL ASBESTOS ABATEMENT AT THE
  SHORB CLINIC – F2M24-21, N2M24-3

  On September 14, 2023, contractor EFI Global Inc. conducted professional pre-demolition
  asbestos and lead paint assessment services for the Shorb Clinic building. Based on the
  assessment, asbestos-containing materials and lead-based paint were identified. The
  planned scope of work includes the completion of a South Coast Air Quality Management
  District (SCAQMD) Procedure 5, which is the initial clean-up of the interior of the building.
  Removing intact identified asbestos-containing materials and pre-demolition stabilization
  of “flaking or peeling” identified Lead Based Paint. The project will be funded with State of
  California funds. The project bids are due no later than 10:30 a.m. on February 15, 2024,
  in the office of the City Clerk and will be opened at 11:00 a.m. that same day.

  Public Comment:  Joyce Amaro, 1808 S. Sixth St., representing the Alhambra
  Preservation Group, expressed concern about the Notice Inviting Bids and asked that the
  item be continued to date after the completion of the Environmental Impact Report for the
  Alhambra Community Center.

  Action Taken:  City Council authorized staff to circulate a Notice Inviting Bids to
  prospective contractors to abate asbestos and lead-based paint from the Shorb Clinic

11.  AUTHORIZING RESOLUTION TO APPROVE THE SUBMITTAL OF AN APPLICATION
  FOR THE WATERSMART SMALL-SCALE WATER EFFICIENCY GRANT PROGRAM
  – F2M24-18, R2M24-1

  The United States Bureau of Reclamation’s WaterSMART Grant Program is accepting
  applications for small-scale water efficiency projects that seek to conserve and better
  manage water supplies. Projects that are supported by an existing water management
  and conservation plan or other planning effort led by the applicant are prioritized. Staff
  have identified a project to replace approximately 330 meters at various locations in the
  City and purchase an online customer portal for a total cost of $200,000. The grant
  proposal includes $100,000 in Federal funding and $100,000 in non-Federal match. The
  grant guidelines require an official resolution by the City Council which provides authority
  to proceed with the application of projects and receipt of grant funds pursuant to the
  Bureau of Reclamation’s policies and procedures. If the project is selected for funding,
  staff will return to the City Council for approval to solicit bids or proposals, appropriate
  grant funds for the proposed projects, and issue notices of completion.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council adopted Resolution No. R2M24-1 entitled: A
  Resolution of the City Council of the City of Alhambra, California approving the authority
  to file an application with the United States Bureau of Reclamation for the WaterSMART
  Small-Scale Water Efficiency Grant Program; and, directed staff to undertake the steps
  necessary to final Council’s action.

  CITY OF ALHAMBRA OFFICIAL ZONING MAP); AND ADOPTION OF A RESOLUTION
  APPROVING GENERAL PLAN TEXT AMENDMENT AMD-23-08 (AN AMENDMENT TO
  THE LAND USE AND COMMUNITY DESIGN CHAPTER OF THE CITY OF ALHAMBRA
  GENERAL PLAN, VISION 2040), GENERAL PLAN MAP AMENDMENT AMD-23-07 (AN
  AMENDMENT TO THE CITY OF ALHAMBRA GENERAL PLAN LAND USE MAP), AND
  INITIAL STUDY/NEGATIVE DECLARATION – F2M20-24, O2M23-4823, R2M23-54

  After receiving staff’s presentation and public testimony at the November 13, 2023 public
  hearing and then continuing the public hearing to the December 11, 2023 meeting, the
  City Council deliberated and determined which of the Planning Commission’s
  recommendations to include and gave first reading to Ordinance No. O2M23-4823
  approving Zoning Text Amendment AMD-23-10 (The Comprehensive Update to the City
  of Alhambra Zoning Code [Title 23 of the Alhambra Municipal Code]) and Zoning Map
  Amendment AMD-23-09 (An Amendment to the City of Alhambra Official Zoning Map).
  Additionally, the Council deliberated and determined which of the Planning Commission’s
  recommendations to include in a Resolution approving General Plan Text Amendment
  AMD-23-08 (An Amendment to the Land Use and Community Design Chapter of the City
  of Alhambra General Plan, Vision 2040), General Plan Map Amendment AMD-23-07 (An
  Amendment to the City of Alhambra General Plan Land Use Map), and adopting the Initial
  Study/Negative Declaration for the Project pursuant to the California Environmental
  Quality Act (CEQA). Staff requested that the City Council introduce O2M23-4823 for its
  second reading and adopt the ordinance as well as adopt the related Resolution
  (R2M23-54).

  Public Comment:

  1.  Jennifer Ng, S. Cordova St., thanked the Council for their vote regarding 21 S.
  Cordova St. and 17 S. Cordova St. being zoned as Residential. She spoke about
  the impacts of the lots currently zoned as Parking being changed to Commercial.

  2.  Lewis McCammon, 105 N. Cordova St., submitted a handout to the Council on file
  in the City Clerk’s Office. He discussed the inclusionary housing aspect of zoning
  code – Chapter 23.15 and a recent op-ed article in the Orange County Register
  regarding selling bonds to fund silent-second mortgages for down payments to
  assist low-income homebuyers.

  3.  Cody Corbett, 217 S. Granada Ave., spoke in favor of 35-feet building heights in
  the East Main Corridor.

  4.  Bernice Ortega, 227 S. El Molino St., spoke against the amendment to the City of
  Alhambra General Plan regarding land use. She expressed concerns regarding
  building heights in the East Main Corridor, construction of the Chinatown Service
  Center and vehicle traffic around the new development project at Monterey Street.

  Discussion: Councilmember LEE made a motion to approve the second reading of the
  ordinance and resolution. Responding to public comment, City Attorney MONTES clarified
  that in the EMC the maximum height is 35 feet, while the 40ft within 50ft height only applies
  to the CMU and AC zones as stipulated in page 39 of the zoning code. Councilmember
  ANDRADE-STADLER and Planning Commissioner Vice Chair GARCIA discussed
  Residential Permit (RPD) process and the Planning Commission’s concerns with the
  projects in zones, such as industrial zones with questionable environmental issues.
  Councilmember PÉREZ and Community Development Director HO responded to Ms. Ng’s
  comments regarding parking lots. Ms. PÉREZ referred to Ms. Andrade-Stadler’s
  comments and suggested that the City use a Conditional Use Permit (CUP) process as
  opposed to the RPD Process. Councilmember MALONEY and Mr. MONTES continued to
  discuss Ms. Pérez’s suggestion and the differences between a CUP process and a RPD
  process with Mr. MONTES. Ms. PÉREZ requested an amendment to the original motion
  to make changes in which Housing projects in the industrial and professional office zones
  would be subject to a CUP instead of an RPD, unless otherwise exempt from that process
  by virtue of being a by-right project, and that with regards to Housing Accountability Act
  compliant projects only objective standards and criteria would be applied for that CUP
  process, consistent with the Housing Accountability Act requirements. Ms. LEE seconded
